tuv.prop: <seg>To Sherlock Holmes she is always the woman.</seg>
<seg>In his eyes she eclipses and predominates the whole of her sex.</seg>
tuv.seg: I have seldom heard him mention her under any other name.
他の呼称などつゆほども聞かない。

tuv.prop: <seg>I have seldom heard him mention her under any other name.</seg>

tuv.seg: In his eyes she eclipses and predominates the whole of her sex.
彼女の前ではどんな女性も影を潜める、とでも考えているのであろう。

tuv.prop: <seg>In his eyes she eclipses and predominates the whole of her sex.</seg>
<seg>All emotions, and that one particularly, were abhorrent to his cold, precise but admirably balanced mind.</seg>
tuv.seg: It was not that he felt any emotion akin to love for Irene Adler.
だがアイリーン・アドラーに恋慕の情といったものを抱いているのではない。

tuv.prop: <seg>It was not that he felt any emotion akin to love for Irene Adler.</seg>
<seg>He was, I take it, the most perfect reasoning and observing machine that the world has seen, but as a lover he would have placed himself in a false position.</seg>
tuv.seg: All emotions, and that one particularly, were abhorrent to his cold, precise but admirably balanced mind.
あらゆる情、とりわけ恋というものは、ホームズの精神にとっては、到底受け入れることができない。精神を冷徹で狂いなく、それでいて偏りがまったくないままに保たねばならないからだ。

tuv.prop: <seg>All emotions, and that one particularly, were abhorrent to his cold, precise but admirably balanced mind.</seg>
<seg>He never spoke of the softer passions, save with a gibe and a sneer.</seg>
tuv.seg: He was, I take it, the most perfect reasoning and observing machine that the world has seen, but as a lover he would have placed himself in a false position.
個人的な考えだが、推理と観察にかけて、ホームズは世界一の完全無欠な機械である。けれども恋愛向きではない。

tuv.prop: <seg>He was, I take it, the most perfect reasoning and observing machine that the world has seen, but as a lover he would have placed himself in a false position.</seg>
<seg>They were admirable things for the observer—excellent for drawing the veil from men’s motives and actions.</seg>
tuv.seg: He never spoke of the softer passions, save with a gibe and a sneer.
斜に構えねば、人の情については語れない。

tuv.prop: <seg>He never spoke of the softer passions, save with a gibe and a sneer.</seg>

<seg>But for the trained reasoner to admit such intrusions into his own delicate and finely adjusted temperament was to introduce a distracting factor which might throw a doubt upon all his mental results.</seg>
tuv.seg: They were admirable things for the observer—excellent for drawing the veil from men’s motives and actions.
観察にはもってこいだ――情こそが人の動機や行動のヴェールをはぎ取る。

tuv.prop: <seg>They were admirable things for the observer—excellent for drawing the veil from men’s motives and actions.</seg>
<seg>Grit in a sensitive instrument, or a crack in one of his own high-power lenses, would not be more disturbing than a strong emotion in a nature such as his.</seg>
tuv.seg: But for the trained reasoner to admit such intrusions into his own delicate and finely adjusted temperament was to introduce a distracting factor which might throw a doubt upon all his mental results.
だが、とぎすまされた推理の場合、ひとたびそのようなものが厳密に調整された心に入りこめば、乱す種となってしまう。そうすればどんな思考の結果も疑わしい。

tuv.prop: <seg>But for the trained reasoner to admit such intrusions into his own delicate and finely adjusted temperament was to introduce a distracting factor which might throw a doubt upon all his mental results.</seg>
<seg>And yet there was but one woman to him, and that woman was the late Irene Adler, of dubious and questionable memory.</seg>
tuv.seg: Grit in a sensitive instrument, or a crack in one of his own high-power lenses, would not be more disturbing than a strong emotion in a nature such as his.
精密機器に砂が混入することよりも、所持する高性能の拡大鏡にひびが入ることよりも、ホームズのような心に強い情緒が芽生えることの方が、悩ましいことなのである。

tuv.prop: <seg>Grit in a sensitive instrument, or a crack in one of his own high-power lenses, would not be more disturbing than a strong emotion in a nature such as his.</seg>
tuv.seg: And yet there was but one woman to him, and that woman was the late Irene Adler, of dubious and questionable memory.
だがそんなホームズにも、ひとりだけ女性というものがあった。その女こそ、かつてのアイリーン・アドラー、まことしやかな噂の多い女だ。
